install.title: Install the web app (PWA)
install.windows: Windows: Open StörDesk in Chrome or Edge. Click the install icon in the address bar (“Install this site as an app”) or “… → Apps → Install this site as an app”.
install.android: Android: Open StörDesk in Chrome. Tap “… → Add to Home screen” or “Install app”.
install.ios: iPhone/iPad: Open StörDesk in Safari. Tap the Share button and then “Add to Home Screen”. Web Push requires the installed app from iOS 16.4.

activate.title: Activate Web Push
activate.hint: After installation: go to Settings → Notifications, open the “Web Push” section and click “Register this device”. Grant the browser permission to show notifications. Push messages will then reach you here.

webpush.title: Web Push (VAPID) — setup guide
webpush.hint: Web Push is switched off by default in StörDesk. The channel sends as soon as all three values are set in the environment of the API:
webpush.why: This is no error, but the intended safe state: every server needs its own key pair, so the push service can attribute the devices to this server unambiguously.
webpush.publicKey: VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY — the public key the browser receives
webpush.privateKey: VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY — the private key with which the VAPID JWT is signed
webpush.subject: VAPID_SUBJECT — the contact address (“mailto:” or “https:”) for the push service
webpush.commandDocker: docker compose exec api npx web-push generate-vapid-keys
webpush.commandHostLabel: In a terminal (Node and npm installed)
webpush.commandDockerLabel: In the Docker stack (in the API container)
webpush.generateHint: Run the command in a terminal that has Node and npm installed (npx is part of npm), or in the API container of the Docker stack. The folder does not matter: the command does not read or start with the project, and it creates a fresh key pair every time. The web container of the stack is nginx and has no Node — the command does not run there ("executable file not found in $PATH"). The command prints the three values (Public Key, Private Key, Subject) — copy all three.
webpush.copyToClipboard: Copy the command to the clipboard
webpush.envHint: Enter the values into your local .env file — never commit them, never build them into the image, and restart the API container (docker compose restart api).
webpush.restartHint: Once the keys are set and the API is restarted: the notice under “Notifications” disappears, the public key reaches the browser and under “Settings → Notifications” the section “Web Push” offers the registration of the devices.
webpush.secret: The private key is a secret: never commit it, never log it, never send it to the browser.
